jobs.location: Palo Alto, CA | Palo Alto, CA, United States
jobs.jd:
About the team: 

 Rubrik secures and accelerates the world’s AI transformation. As AI agents reshape the enterprise, Rubrik’s Enterprise AI Incubation team proves it on Rubrik itself.
We are building a thinking enterprise: applications that don't just record the business but help run it. They learn from our data, act through our own agents, and improve with every decision. 
Fully backed by executive leadership, this team drives meaningful, large-scale enterprise transformation.

About the role:

 We want senior engineers who have already shipped agents that real people rely on, and who are ready to do it again at higher stakes. You will drop into the real work, redesign it around agents that carry it end to end, and ship it as the new way that part of Rubrik operates.You’ll own your agent systems end to end: understanding the workflow, designing the architecture, writing the code, deploying, and running it in production. Rather than simply querying an API, you engineer robust, production-grade infrastructure around model endpoints, integrating custom tooling, context pipelines, automated evaluations, and defensive guardrails to ensure resilience against unstructured real-world data.

 You also decide whether a problem needs an agent, a simpler automation, or nothing at all, and you have explicit authority to stop or re-scope work that won’t deliver impact. You thrive in ambiguous environments with a low-ego mindset, leveraging AI coding tools as core collaborative partners in your engineering workflow.

What you’ll do:

- Lead product discovery alongside Product Managers and domain experts to understand real workflows, map them out, and define clear problems, baselines, and success criteria as the foundation for building agentic solutions.

- Design, build, test, and deploy production agents, automations, and internal tools using coding agents, LLM APIs, and agent frameworks, integrated with Rubrik’s internal agent platform and business systems.

- Turn complex processes into multi-agent workflows that carry real work and make decisions: orchestrators that qualify and routes deals, workers that move orders through approval and fulfillment under business rules, agents that monitor signals and recommend actions for customer health, or coordinated agents that handle hire-to-retire steps across HR, IT, and managers with shared state and clear handoffs.

- Engineer agents for autonomy with reliability, including tool and orchestration flows, context management, caching, retries, and failure handling.

- Leverage full-stack engineering across backend services, APIs, data models, interactive screens, approval UIs, and chat interfaces as the complete medium to deliver high-ownership, user-facing agent systems.

- Apply solid software engineering practices to AI systems, treating prompts, skills, configs, and specs as versioned artifacts, with code review, tests, CI or CD, and staged rollouts.

- Implement evaluation, guardrails, and quality control: derive evals from workflow data, establish quality gates and guardrails, integrate human-in-the-loop approvals where needed, and monitor production runs to refine agents over time.

- Use measured results to decide how to evolve or retire agents, and turn successful systems into patterns and libraries that can be reused.

Experience you’ll need:

- Around 7 or more years of professional software engineering experience in production systems, and around 2 or more years of professional, hands-on experience building AI agents and agent powered production applications with measurable outcomes.

- Strong full stack engineering background, with a track record of designing, building, and owning services end to end, including backend APIs and integrations, data models, and user facing interfaces such as approval UIs, dashboards, or chat surfaces.

- A builder mindset: comfortable defining baselines and metrics, reporting results in business terms, working in a fast moving environment, and closing the loop by building, demoing, learning, and building again. If you like seeing improvements in hours saved, errors avoided, and teams unblocked, you will have plenty of chances to measure that here.

Software engineering skills and best practices:

- System design: break down complex problems, design APIs and data models, reason about latency, throughput, and failure modes, and choose simple, robust architectures.

- Algorithms, data structures, access control permissions, and data provenance.

- Spec driven development: turn vague requirements into clear problem statements, write or refine design docs, and use a Spec → Plan → Task → Code→ Converge flow so work is traceable from design to code, including when you use AI coding agents.

- Execution discipline: use version control, code review, automated tests, CI or CD, staged rollouts and rollbacks, logging, metrics, and tracing, and improve systems based on issues and signals from production.

AI engineering skills and best practices:

- Build agents in code using LLM APIs, SDKs, and libraries, not just no code or low code tools, and have shipped agentic systems that real users rely on.

- Design robust agent harnesses and multi agent orchestrations: model tools and resources, manage context and state, and keep runs reliable under real world data and load.

- Establish continuous evaluation and safety mechanisms: turn production failures into test cases, gate changes on eval suite results, and enforce guardrails across agent workflows.

- Exercise clear judgment on AI fit: decide when a problem needs an agent versus a simpler automation or no build, and make tradeoffs around model choice, latency and cost, context strategy, and autonomy using data rather than intuition.

Preferred qualifications:

- Knowledge/context graphs: entities and relationships, GraphRAG, hybrid retrieval.

- Agent frameworks and runtimes: Google ADK, LangGraph, OpenAI style, cloud or container platforms.

- Lead a technical team and own customer and team engagement 

- Travels to client sites for projects, estimated 50-75%

- Maintain billable utilisation targets for your team

 About Salesforce 
 Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.
 
 Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

 The Experience 

The Senior Forward Deployed Engineer is part of Salesforce's delivery organisation, responsible for designing, building, and deploying agentic AI solutions directly inside enterprise customer environments. In this role, you will work as part of a delivery pod — partnering closely with a Deployment Strategist to co-build solutions that go live in production environments from day one, spanning configuration, customisation, and full-stack deployment across some of the largest enterprises in the world.

We are looking for a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer who brings a builder mindset, strong production-grade engineering experience, and the ability to own and deliver complex technical components — someone who ships quality code, contributes to team knowledge, and leaves customer teams more capable after every engagement.

 What You'll Actually Be Doing 

- Design and build AI agents and experiences that take real actions for real organisations — owning technical components end-to-end from architecture choice through to deployed, validated, and observable in production, including agent intelligence design, prompts, reasoning, tool calls, and integration with customer systems.

- Build and integrate data pipelines on Salesforce Data Cloud, Snowflake, Databricks, and customer data platforms, and maintain agent performance dashboards and customer Key Performance Indicator (KPI) reporting to track deployment health and business outcomes.

- Contribute to and help lead Proofs of Concept (PoC) and Minimum Viable Products (MVP) that move from concept to deployable in days — co-building alongside customers and partners and sharing best practices as you go.

- Surface platform gaps, edge cases, and field insights to senior engineers and product teams — partnering with the Deployment Strategist in your pod to translate customer business challenges into agentic solutions that actually ship.

Citi Equities Technology | Equities Electronic Execution (Electronic Trading)

 Role Overview
 Citi's Equities Technology organization is seeking a Senior Software Engineer – Ultra Low Latency Risk Engine Lead Developer to join the Equities Electronic Execution (Electronic Trading) technology team. This role is focused on the design, development, and delivery of Citi's next-generation low-latency Risk Engine for cash equities and its integration into the broader execution platform — encompassing the Centralised Position Service, Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data processing.

 The engineer will own critical, latency-sensitive risk-checking components that sit directly in the cash equities trading hot path, ensuring pre-trade and real-time risk controls are enforced with microsecond-level performance while maintaining correctness and resiliency at scale. This is a hands-on, deeply technical role that also carries leadership responsibilities — mentoring engineers, driving architecture decisions, and coordinating delivery across global development centers.

 The person will collaborate closely with product development, quantitative research, technology infrastructure, production support, and QA teams, with close alignment to global strategy and cross-regional delivery (APAC, EMEA, NAM).

 Responsibilities
 Risk Engine & Core Development 
 
- Design, develop, and maintain the ultra low-latency, in-line Risk Engine responsible for real-time pre-trade risk checks, position limits, and exposure controls across cash equities electronic execution flows.
 
- Architect and optimize high-performance, lock-minimal, multi-threaded components capable of processing risk decisions in the sub-microsecond to low-microsecond range.
 
- Integrate risk and position components with Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data feed handlers.
 
- Apply deep expertise in JVM performance tuning, memory management, garbage collection avoidance, and/or native (C++/Rust) performance engineering to eliminate latency outliers ("jitter") in the risk path.
 
- Perform system-level performance tuning to minimize end-to-end latency and jitter across the risk and execution path.
 
 Qualifications
 
- 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on experience building risk management, position-keeping, or other latency-critical systems for cash equities electronic trading or algorithmic trading platforms at a global investment bank or equivalent financial institution.

- Must have strong Java skills 
 
- Strong, hands-on technical expertise in Low Latency Java and/or C++ (Rust a plus), including multi-threading, concurrency, lock-free data structures, Java NIO, and JVM/GC performance tuning.
 
- Hands-on experience with low-latency messaging and IPC frameworks such as Aeron, Solace, or equivalent shared-memory/IPC technologies for building distributed, high-throughput trading systems.
 
- Demonstrated background in real-time distributed risk management systems for cash equities flow products , including asynchronous, event-driven architectures.
 
- Practical, hands-on experience with NUMA-aware design, CPU core pinning/affinity and isolation, Linux kernel/OS tuning, and low-latency networking (kernel bypass, RDMA, or specialized NIC tuning) for ultra low-latency, high-throughput systems.
 
- Strong understanding of automated testing techniques, test-driven development, and quality engineering practices for mission-critical systems.
 
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present and grasp complex technical and risk concepts in a multicultural, cross-regional environment, and to work effectively with globally distributed stakeholders (trading desks, quants, infrastructure, and support teams).
 
- Working knowledge of regional exchange microstructure and relevant regulatory regimes governing cash equities electronic trading and risk controls.
 Education

jobs.jd:
Citi Equities Technology | Equities Electronic Execution (Electronic Trading)

Role Overview
 Citi's Equities Technology organization is seeking a Senior Software Engineer – Ultra Low Latency Risk Engine Lead Developer to join the Equities Electronic Execution (Electronic Trading) technology team. This role is focused on the design, development, and delivery of Citi's next-generation low-latency Risk Engine for cash equities and its integration into the broader execution platform — encompassing the Centralised Position Service, Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data processing.
 The engineer will own critical, latency-sensitive risk-checking components that sit directly in the cash equities trading hot path, ensuring pre-trade and real-time risk controls are enforced with microsecond-level performance while maintaining correctness and resiliency at scale. This is a hands-on, deeply technical role that also carries leadership responsibilities — mentoring engineers, driving architecture decisions, and coordinating delivery across global development centers.
 The person will collaborate closely with product development, quantitative research, technology infrastructure, production support, and QA teams, with close alignment to global strategy and cross-regional delivery (APAC, EMEA, NAM).

Responsibilities

 Risk Engine & Core Development 
 
- Design, develop, and maintain the ultra low-latency, in-line Risk Engine responsible for real-time pre-trade risk checks, position limits, and exposure controls across cash equities electronic execution flows.
 
- Architect and optimize high-performance, lock-minimal, multi-threaded components capable of processing risk decisions in the sub-microsecond to low-microsecond range.
 
- Integrate risk and position components with Client Connectivity, Market Access layers, and high-throughput market data feed handlers.
 
- Apply deep expertise in JVM performance tuning, memory management, garbage collection avoidance, and/or native (C++/Rust) performance engineering to eliminate latency outliers ("jitter") in the risk path.
 
- Perform system-level performance tuning to minimize end-to-end latency and jitter across the risk and execution path.

Qualifications
 
- 10+ years of overall software engineering experience, with substantial hands-on experience building risk management, position-keeping, or other latency-critical systems for cash equities electronic trading or algorithmic trading platforms at a global investment bank or equivalent financial institution.
 
- Strong, hands-on technical expertise in Low Latency Java and/or C++ (Rust a plus), including multi-threading, concurrency, lock-free data structures, Java NIO, and JVM/GC performance tuning.
 
- Hands-on experience with low-latency messaging and IPC frameworks such as Aeron, Solace, or equivalent shared-memory/IPC technologies for building distributed, high-throughput trading systems.
 
- Demonstrated background in real-time distributed risk management systems for cash equities flow products , including asynchronous, event-driven architectures.
 
- Practical, hands-on experience with NUMA-aware design, CPU core pinning/affinity and isolation, Linux kernel/OS tuning, and low-latency networking (kernel bypass, RDMA, or specialized NIC tuning) for ultra low-latency, high-throughput systems.
 
- Strong understanding of automated testing techniques, test-driven development, and quality engineering practices for mission-critical systems.
 
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to present and grasp complex technical and risk concepts in a multicultural, cross-regional environment, and to work effectively with globally distributed stakeholders (trading desks, quants, infrastructure, and support teams).
 
- Working knowledge of regional exchange microstructure and relevant regulatory regimes governing cash equities electronic trading and risk controls.

Education
 
- Bachelor's degree / University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience (e.g., Mechanical Engineering combined with a Diploma in Advanced Computing).

In return, we’ll give you the trust to take risks, the tools to grow, the skills to develop and the support of a company invested in you for the long haul. So, if you want to inspire a brighter work day for everyone, including yourself, you’ve found a match in Workday, and we hope to be a match for you too.

Agent Factory is where Workday’s next chapter gets built.  Charles River Development is looking for an experienced Azure Infrastructure, Network, DevOps & Infrastructure as Code Engineer to join the Cloud Platform Engineering team. In this role, you will design, build, automate, and operate secure enterprise-scale Azure infrastructure and networking platforms. You will help modernize cloud delivery through DevOps practices, reusable IaC modules, automation, and strong operational engineering discipline.
 
 Why This Role Is Important to Us 
 The team you will be joining is part of Charles River Development (CRD), which became part of State Street in 2018. CRD develops enterprise investment management software solutions for leading global financial institutions across institutional investment, wealth management, and hedge funds. Together, we created the industry's first open front-to-back platform, State Street Alpha, launched in 2019.
 Join us if delivering next-generation infrastructure, cloud networking, platform automation, deployment reliability, and secure-by-default cloud services using Azure, DevOps, Kubernetes, and Infrastructure as Code sounds like a challenge you are ready for.
 
 What You Will Be Responsible For 
 
- Design, deploy, and support enterprise Azure infrastructure across multiple subscriptions, landing zones, and environments.

- Build and maintain secure Azure networking solutions, including virtual networks, hub-and-spoke architectures, ExpressRoute, VPN Gateway, Azure Firewall, NSGs, routing, DNS, Private Endpoints, Application Gateway, and load balancing.

- Develop, maintain, and improve Infrastructure as Code solutions using Terraform, Bicep, ARM Templates .

- Create reusable IaC modules, deployment patterns, and platform standards that improve consistency, security, and developer experience.

- Build and support CI/CD pipelines using Azure DevOps, Git, YAML pipelines, approvals, variable groups, service connections, and deployment automation .

- Automate operational tasks, infrastructure provisioning, validation, troubleshooting, and reporting using PowerShell, Python, Azure CLI, and REST APIs .

- Support and improve AKS and container platform capabilities, including networking, ingress, identity integration, monitoring, and secure deployment patterns.

- Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, network connectivity, deployment pipeline, identity, DNS, and performance issues across Azure IaaS and PaaS services.

- Create and maintain technical architecture diagrams, design documents, operational runbooks, engineering standards, and knowledge-sharing material.

- Collaborate with application, security, operations, and architecture teams to deliver scalable, reliable, secure, and automated cloud platform capabilities.

- Balance pragmatism with long-term platform vision by continuously improving infrastructure reliability, automation, security posture, and operational processes.

 What We Value 
 
- Strong hands-on experience designing, implementing, and supporting Azure infrastructure in enterprise environments.

- Deep understanding of Azure networking concepts such as routing, DNS, firewalls, private connectivity, segmentation, NSGs, load balancing, and hybrid connectivity.

- Experience codifying cloud platform provisioning using Terraform, Bicep, ARM Templates, Ansible, or equivalent automation tooling.

- Strong DevOps experience with Azure DevOps, Git workflows, CI/CD design, release automation, environment controls, and deployment governance.

- Hands-on scripting and automation experience with PowerShell, Python, Azure CLI, and API-based automation.

- Experience supporting Azure platform services such as Virtual Machines, Virtual Networks, Storage Accounts, Key Vault, AKS, App Services, API Management, Azure SQL, and Log Analytics.

- Understanding of identity, access, and platform security concepts including RBAC, Managed Identity, service principals, network isolation, Conditional Access, and least privilege.

- Experience supporting Windows and Linux-based infrastructure and troubleshooting operating system, platform, and network-level issues.

- Experience implementing secure deployment and operational practices in regulated, audit-focused, or enterprise-scale environments.

- Ability to assist, contribute, and lead when required with prototyping new platform capabilities, network patterns, automation frameworks, and DevOps improvements.

- Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, oral communication, and written communication skills.

- Ability to collaborate with technical staff across multiple systems, disciplines, time zones, and organizational boundaries.

 Education & Preferred Qualifications 
 
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field.

- 10+ years of Azure platform engineering / cloud infrastructure experience 

- Azure certifications such as Azure Administrator Associate, Azure Network Engineer Associate, Azure DevOps Engineer Expert, Azure Solutions Architect Expert are preferred.

- CCNA / CCNP as good-to-have

- Hands-on experience delivering large-scale Azure infrastructure deployments, cloud networking, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform/Bicep), and automated platform provisioning across enterprise environments.

- Experience with financial services, regulated environments, change management, security audit processes, or large-scale enterprise cloud platforms is a plus.

 Additional Requirements 
 
- Comfortable working in a global, distributed engineering environment.

- Self-motivated, accountable, delivery-focused, and able to drive technical initiatives independently.

- Passionate about automation, cloud engineering, operational excellence, secure infrastructure, and continuous improvement.

- Ability to document engineering decisions clearly and contribute to team knowledge sharing and collaboration.

jobs.jd:
Job Description: 
 Job Title: Lead Engineer, VP 
 Location: Pune, India 
 Corporate Title: Vice President 
 
 Role Description 
 Overview:
 
- Corporate Banking is a technology centric business, with an increasing move to real-time processing, an increasing appetite from customers for integrated systems and access to supporting data. This means that technology is more important than ever for business.

- Deutsche Bank is one of the few banks with the scale and network to compete aggressively in this space, and the breadth of investment in this area is unmatched by our peers. Joining the team is a unique opportunity to help rebuild the core of some of our most mission critical processing systems from the ground-up.

- Our Corporate Bank Technology team is a global team across 30 countries. The primary businesses that we support within Corporate Bank are Cash Management, Securities Services, Trade Finance and Trust & Agency Services. CB Technology supports these businesses through ‘vertical’ CIO aligned teams and by ‘horizontals’ such as Client Connectivity, Surveillance and Regulatory, Infrastructure, Architecture, Production, and Risk & Control.
 About Role:
 
- As the Lead Engineer of the Channel Security team, you will be responsible for the development and end-to-end technical delivery of a mission-critical platform designed to protect the Corporate Bank’s online channels from real-time fraud. You are expected to be a hands-on backend developer with deep architectural expertise to meet demanding performance, reliability, and security requirements, while also providing coaching and technical guidance to the development squad to enable their success.
 
 What we’ll offer you 
 As part of our flexible scheme, here are just some of the benefits that you’ll enjoy
 
- Best in class leave policy

- Gender neutral parental leaves

- 100% reimbursement under childcare assistance benefit (gender neutral)

- Sponsorship for Industry relevant certifications and education

- Employee Assistance Program for you and your family members

- Comprehensive Hospitalization Insurance for you and your dependents

- Accident and Term life Insurance

- Complementary Health screening for 35 yrs. and above
 
 Your key responsibilities 
 
- Provide technical leadership and mentorship to the team, foster a culture of engineering excellence and ownership.

- Lead by example through direct, hands-on development of the core services and critical components of the Fraud Monitoring Platform.

- Partner closely with the platform architect to define and drive the implementation of the solution design, ensuring the Fraud Monitoring Platform is scalable, resilient, and secure.

- Work closely with Engineering Heads, Project Management, and leaders of related platforms to build, integrate, and deliver the software.

- Drive continuous improvement in the team's performance across the entire SDLC, including code quality, automated testing (QA), CI/CD pipelines, and post-release operational activities.

- Act as the primary technical expert on the platform in strategy meetings, stakeholder discussions, and future product development opportunities.

- Partner with SRE and L3 support teams to proactively identify and implement architectural improvements that enhance system reliability and reduce operational toil.
 
 Your skills and experience 
 
- Proven, hands-on experience designing, building, and deploying complex, scalable applications on a major public cloud platform (GCP strongly preferred).

- Extensive hands-on backend programming experience, with expert-level proficiency in the modern Java ecosystem (Java 17+, Spring Boot).

- Familiarity with AI/ML, Generative AI and agentic AI patterns, with an understanding of how ML models, LLMs or AI agents can be safely integrated and orchestrated within enterprise and real-time decisioning platforms.

- Experience applying AI-assisted engineering techniques across software development, testing, operational support or developer productivity is required.

- Overall experience of 15+ years in software engineering, with a proven track record of leading the design and delivery of complex, business-critical systems.

- Strong knowledge of Microservices Architecture, Kubernetes, Docker, and building cloud-native applications.

- Proficiency with event-driven architecture and messaging systems like Kafka or MQ.

- Expertise with relational databases (Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL) and in-memory data stores/caches (Redis).

- Good understanding of Git, CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions), and DevOps/SRE principles.

- Experience engineering systems with high-load and high-traffic requirements, including performance testing, tuning, and ensuring zero-downtime releases.

- A strong understanding of modern security principles, including API security (mTLS, OAuth2), data protection, and secure coding practices.

- Familiarity with the principles of AI/ML and an understanding of how to integrate and orchestrate machine learning models or AI agents within a real-time decisioning system is a strong plus.
 
 Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimise workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs. 
 
 How we’ll support you 
 
- Training and development to help you excel in your career

- Coaching and support from experts in your team

- A culture of continuous learning to aid progression

- A range of flexible benefits that you can tailor to suit your needs
 
 About us and our teams 
 Please visit our company website for further information:
 https://www.db.com/company/company.html 
 
 We strive for a culture in which we are empowered to excel together every day. This includes acting responsibly, thinking commercially, taking initiative and working collaboratively.
 Together we share and celebrate the successes of our people. Together we are Deutsche Bank Group.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer II
jobs.jd:
Who we are 

 Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 

 Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. 

 About this role: 

 Commercial Navigation helps fleets turn planned work into guided trips that are safe, efficient, and visible to the people running the operation. We build navigation inside the Samsara Driver app and the supporting experiences around it: mobile guidance on the road, session review for fleet managers, fuel-aware routing, and safety-focused improvements that show up where drivers actually drive. The team has a real foundation in production, and there is still a lot of greenfield ahead as we expand what navigation means for commercial fleets. 

 We are looking for a product-minded senior engineer who can own ambiguous problems end to end, make practical tradeoffs across surfaces, and ship work that holds up in the field. You will contribute across mobile, backend services, and web as needed, with judgment about what matters most for customers rather than a fixed layer of the stack. This is a deeply technical problem space that blends real-time data, thoughtful UX, and platform-wide coordination to create a seamless experience under challenging conditions, like poor connectivity, dynamic job schedules, and constantly changing routes.

 This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US and Canada. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

 You should apply if: 

- You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

- You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.

- You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.

- You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we’re all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win – together.

 In this role, you will: 

- Own Features End to End: Take full ownership of navigation initiatives from design through production rollout, including follow-up on quality, adoption, and customer impact after launch.

- Deliver with High Engineering Standards: Write maintainable, well-tested code and hold a high bar in design and code review. Use modern development tools, including AI-assisted workflows, with sound judgment. Improve observability, testing, and the systems that keep navigation reliable in production.

- Build Across the Product: Design and ship features across mobile, backend services, and web—driver navigation experiences, admin visibility, optimized routing, and safety-focused navigation capabilities.

- Turn Ambiguity into Action: Clarify what you are building and why: learn from fleet managers and drivers, align with the product team on priorities, define success metrics, plan milestones, and raise risks and tradeoffs before they become surprises.

- Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work closely with engineers, product managers, designers, and partners in Maps, Telematics, and adjacent teams to deliver cohesive navigation experiences end to end.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

 Minimum requirements for the role: 

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience 

- 6+ years of experience

- Proven experience shipping customer-facing software in production across multiple surfaces (e.g. mobile, web, and/or backend services), with depth in at least one and the ability to contribute effectively in the others.

- Comfortable using AI development tools with judgment in day-to-day engineering

 An ideal candidate also has: 

- Experience building mobile applications, including React Native. At Samsara we also use Swift and Kotlin for native modules and in-cab experiences . 

- Experience shipping and maintaining features over several years, demonstrating long-term ownership . 

- Domain expertise in logistics, or industrial IoT, especially building mobile apps for drivers or field workers or familiarity with geospatial or mapping technologies.

jobs.jd:
The Opportunity 
 
 Typography is central to how ideas are communicated. If you're passionate about beautifully created design, have deep curiosity about what AI can do, and take personal responsibility for creating products that people love; then this may be the role for you. Adobe Fonts supports millions of creatives in choosing and using typefaces across fonts.adobe.com, Express, Photoshop, Illustrator, Acrobat, and more Creative Cloud platforms. Our Internal Services team provides the platform engineering and deployment backbone for all of these. We manage CI/CD, deployment approaches, the services and data layers our engineers depend on, our observability and security stance, and increasingly the agentic tools that transform how our entire organization delivers software.
 
 We're seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to lead this exciting journey in our San Francisco location.
 
 What you'll do 
 
- Own and evolve our deployment platform. Lead strategy for CI/CD, PR environments, and release safety across a mixed fleet that includes containerized services, serverless services, and static front ends.

- Build the foundation for AI-accelerated development. Help build our agent factory and grow our internal agentic toolkit and skill library.

- Ship inference applications at scale. Take greenfield services from spec to production and standardize our ML/inference footprint.

- Modernize our services for the AI era. Identify where an existing service is held back by its current build and lead the fix.

- Rethink our security posture for agentic threats. Lead how we secure autonomous agents and their tool use.

- Expose Adobe Fonts to the agentic ecosystem. Extend our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and conversational, intent-based font discovery.

- Work higher up the stack, too. Contribute directly to search, browse, discovery, and the customer-facing experiences our platform powers.

- Hold ownership over what you deliver to production, encompassing on-call support, incident management, and the reliability of the services and pipelines that the entire organization depends upon.

- Set technical direction and multiply the team. Write the development docs, run the technical reviews, and mentor engineers.
 
 What we're looking for 
 
 Software engineering 
 
- Deep full-stack fundamentals and craft — build, testing, code quality, code review — plus system development and production maturity: latency, scale, reliability, observability, and on-call ownership.

- Ships and owns services end to end, and reasons fluently across the whole stack: front end (JavaScript/TypeScript, React or Web Components), application services (Ruby/Rails, Python, Go, and comfort picking up others), and the SRE/config/hardware layer beneath (Terraform, Chef, Kubernetes/Helm, AWS).
 
 Platform & deployment depth 
 
- Strong CI/CD ownership (Jenkins or equivalent), containerization and orchestration, infrastructure-as-code, and AWS (EC2/ASG, IAM, Lambda, API Gateway, CloudFront). Experience making deployment fast, safe, and self-service — ephemeral/preview environments, progressive delivery, rollback strategy.

- Solid grasp of the data and messaging layers behind real services, including relational, caching, search, and event-driven/pub-sub. You know how to run migrations and upgrades without downtime.
 
 AI/agentic proficiency 
 
- Hands-on understanding of building AI-enabled systems: agent runtimes, tool calling, MCP, LLM/inference serving, and the infrastructure around them — evaluation, feedback loops, observability, and sandboxed execution.

- A security outlook for this new surface — you think about how agentic systems fail and get abused, and proactively build guardrails accordingly.
 
 Leadership & scope 
 
- Track record of delivering high-impact platform work used across multiple teams, leading complex cross-team technical efforts, and balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, security, and operability.

- Excellent written and verbal communication.

- Typically 12+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated senior-level impact.
 
 Nice to have 
 
- Ruby on Rails at scale, and experience decomposing or modernizing a large monolith.

- GPU/model-serving infrastructure and low-latency inference (e.g. SageMaker, Kubernetes GPU platforms); search-engine internals (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, vector/hybrid search).

- Experience building developer platforms, internal tooling, or agent harnesses adopted by other teams.

- Event-driven architectures and secrets-management platforms (Vault, CyberArk).

- Front-end depth with modern component systems (Web Components/Lit, React/TypeScript, build systems).

jobs.title: Lead Site Reliability Engineer
jobs.jd:
As a Lead Site Reliability Engineer at JPMorgan Chase in Infrastructure Platforms, you are a code-first software engineer specializing in reliability. You will design and build the automation, tooling, and observability that keep enterprise-scale platforms resilient, and you own those systems end-to-end, including SLIs/SLOs, incident leadership, and toil reduction. You will write software that makes enterprise-scale infrastructure reliable, observable, and self-healing. You will work AI-native, using AI fluently across the software development lifecycle to build faster, respond to incidents quicker, and engineer away manual operations, while retaining full accountability for correctness, security, reliability, and cost. 

 Job Responsibilities 

- 
 Engineer reliability into enterprise-scale platforms by writing production software: automation, control loops, self-healing, and tooling that remove manual operations rather than institutionalise them 

- 
 Build systems around declarative, intent-based design: model the desired state as data in a trusted source of truth and let automation continuously reconcile reality to it, rather than driving change through imperative, one-off scripts 

- 
 Treat data as a first-class reliability asset: instrument, collect, and reason over telemetry and state data to drive detection, diagnosis, and closed-loop remediation 

- 
 Define and operationalize SLIs and SLOs with stakeholders; implement SLO-based alerting, telemetry standards, and actionable observability 

- 
 Own services end-to-end, taking accountability for reliability, performance, security, and cost, and building operability and observability in from the start

About Us

 At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

 At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

 Available Locations: 

- United States: Atlanta, GA; Austin, TX; Denver, CO; Seattle, WA; Washington DC

- United Kingdom: London

- Portugal: Lisbon

- Canada: Toronto

 About the team 

 Cloudflare Browser Isolation runs web content in remote browsers, helping protect users from threats while preserving a responsive browsing experience. Our team builds the Chromium-based browsing engine, remote rendering and streaming technology, and distributed services that manage browser sessions across Cloudflare’s global network.

 You will work at the intersection of systems programming, distributed systems, and security. Engineers contribute across the product, collaborating on browser changes, service orchestration, observability, and build infrastructure.

 Scope and growth 

 At this level, you will be accountable for outcomes across a problem area that may span several components. You will establish technical direction, make uncertainty and trade-offs explicit, and help other engineers succeed while remaining hands-on. This is an individual-contributor role; people-management experience is not required.

 Technologies we use 

- Browser engine: Chromium and C++.

- Systems programming: Rust.

- Distributed services and orchestration: Go, TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers, Nomad, and Consul.

- Remote rendering and streaming: WebRTC and Skia.

- Browser client: TypeScript, WebAssembly, and WebGL.

 What you will do 

- Lead complex, multi-component initiatives from problem definition and design through implementation, staged rollout, and measurable production outcomes.

- Design and implement changes in our Chromium-based C++ browser and the distributed services and systems components supporting remote browsing, working across Go, Rust, and TypeScript.

- Make and explain architectural trade-offs across latency, availability, resource efficiency, security boundaries, and operational complexity.

- Investigate difficult cross-layer failures and performance bottlenecks, distinguishing browser, host, network, and control-plane causes.

- Improve resilience, capacity management, observability, and release safety; define success metrics and validate results.

- Coordinate work with partner teams, surface dependencies and risks early, and guide delivery through ambiguity.

- Mentor engineers and raise the quality of code reviews, design reviews, testing, documentation, and operational practices.

- Participate in the team’s production on-call rotation after onboarding, lead technical incident investigations as needed, and drive durable corrective actions.

 This role may require flexibility to be on-call outside of standard working hours to address technical issues as needed.

 Desirable Skills, Knowledge, and Experience 

- Strong production C++ proficiency, including memory and resource ownership, concurrency, and debugging in substantial codebases.

- A track record of independently leading complex systems or distributed-service improvements across multiple components, from an unclear problem to a reliable production outcome.

- Strong Linux/UNIX and networking fundamentals, with experience diagnosing correctness, latency, and resource-consumption issues using profiling and operational evidence.

- Experience designing and operating distributed systems, with sound judgment about service boundaries, data partitioning, consistency, timeouts and retries, backpressure, capacity limits, and recovery from partial failures.

- Experience designing safe rollout and recovery strategies and maintaining production software over its lifecycle.

- Ability to communicate trade-offs clearly, align stakeholders, mentor teammates, and improve engineering practices through constructive feedback.

- A willingness to work across C++, Rust, Go, and TypeScript and learn unfamiliar parts of the stack.

 Bonus Points 

 These are preferred qualifications, not prerequisites. Prior Browser Isolation or Cloudflare experience is not required.

- Browser engines, Chromium, browser sandboxing, or security-sensitive systems.

- Low-latency streaming, graphics, remote computing, or other real-time systems.

- Container and workload orchestration, including Nomad or Kubernetes, and service discovery.

- Experience using Rust for systems programming or distributed services.

- Go or TypeScript; WebRTC, Skia, WebAssembly, or WebGL.

- Production observability, capacity planning, incident response, or build and rel

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Data Foundations
jobs.jd:
This is Adyen 

 Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for global customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft, making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition. We create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by a culture that encourages ownership and provides the support to truly own your career. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team, delivering innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster.

 Data Foundations 

 Adyen is building a top-tier data team across San Francisco and Amsterdam. The goal is to accelerate data as our most differentiating and least replicable asset across our company. We are focusing on the foundations: the things that make data work as one thing. We decide how it fits together, what it means, and how anyone, human or AI, can trust and use it.

 The team is new and sits at the heart of our engineering organization. You will join as one of its technical leaders. You will architect data and work on complex challenges across the company, multiplying your impact through the teams and people you work with. You win them over with good design, working prototypes and trust. By driving decisions through ambiguity, you will shape the next generation of Ayden's data.

 You will be based in San Francisco and work closely with the Data Foundations lead in Amsterdam. You will have a lot of room to run your own week.

 What you will do 

- Build greenfield. The mandate, the architecture and the standards are being written now. You help write them.

- Design the foundation. Set the target architecture for shared data models, data contracts and the semantic layer that every domain builds on.

- Give every metric one clear meaning. Work with domain teams so each core metric is defined once and owned by the domain that creates it. Variants get their own names.

- Make data contracts the norm. Agree contracts between producers and consumers, with owners, versions and automatic checks. Consumers are never surprised.

- Build lineage in from the start. Anyone can trace a figure to its source without asking the engineer who built the pipeline.

- Help teams ship data products. Guide domain teams to publish datasets with a clear owner, schema and service level. They own the product. You own the standard.

- Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, review designs and solve hard problems in the data stack.

- Partner across Adyen. Product, Finance, Compliance, Platform Engineering and domain leads. Win the argument with data and a working prototype.

- Grow other engineers. Mentor engineers in Data Foundations and in the domains. Help them solve problems with their own ideas, and raise the bar in design reviews.

 Who you are 

- You have 10+ years in data engineering or data architecture, and you have worked at Staff scope. You have set direction for more than one team, and you are still hands on.

- You pick your own problems. You see what needs to change and drive it to done without being told.

- You have designed shared data models, data contracts or semantic layers that many teams build on, and you can defend the trade-offs.

- You have changed what other teams built without any authority over them. You did it with data, prototypes and trust.

- You explain hard ideas in plain words to engineers, finance people and executives. You write clearly.

- You work well with Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance and other stakeholders, across time zones.

 This role's annual base salary range is $258–$367k, plus RSUs. To learn more about our compensation philosophy, please click here . 

 Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion at Adyen 

 We actively seek different perspectives to sharpen our ideas. Our unique culture is a product of our diverse backgrounds and experiences. No matter who you are or where you’re from, you’re welcome to be your true self at Adyen. 

 If you need accommodations or support during the recruitment process to perform at your best, you’ll have the opportunity to let our team know in your application. We encourage people from all backgrounds and abilities to apply. 

 What’s next? 

 Ensuring a smooth and enjoyable candidate experience is critical for us. We aim to get back to you regarding your application within 5 business days. Our interview process tends to take about 4 weeks to complete, but may fluctuate depending on the role. Learn more about our hiring process here . Don’t be afraid to let us know if you need more flexibility. 

 Adyen is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, national origin, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status or any legally protected status. 

 All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines. 

 San Francisco 

 Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. 

 This role is based out of our San Francisco office. We are an office-first company and value in-person collaboration; we do not offer remote-only roles.

Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. Our mission is to increase the freedom of money and financial access for people around the world.

 About the Role
As a Software Engineer - Blockchain Security at Binance, you will focus on the security of blockchain projects across the BNB Smart Chain (BSC) as well as other chains. It is a unique opportunity to contribute to the field and contribute to the blockchain community.
 
You will work hand-in-hand with various talented workers from Binance on the cutting-edge of crypto to guard safety across many projects and systems. You will also coordinate with other teams aside from the security group, which could provide you an in-depth understanding of the crypto world.

Responsibilities

- Responsible for security related products planning and design, establishing the technical road-map, and completing the construction and coding implementation of important modules and core frameworks.

- Define and implement architecture standards and best practices, responsible for underlying infrastructure / architecture maintenance, develop / maintain tools that automate operational activities and improve engineering productivity, provide automated continuous delivery and on-demand capacity management solutions.

- Responsible for direct user requirements engagement, forming corresponding APIs for client delivery, and maintaining customer relationships. Continuously improve customer satisfaction.

- Identify and solve technical issues in back-end systems, ensuring system performance and stability.

- Performance tuning, online incidents troubleshooting, and system refactoring, optimize the products to maximize speed and scale.

- Design and build libraries and frameworks that will be further used by internal clients, speed up development efficiency and improve code quality.

Requirements

- Currently enrolled or holding a bachelor's degree (or higher) in Computer Science or a related field.

- At least 4-5 years of full stack development experience in a similar role supporting large scale production systems, preferably 2-3 years in the Crypto or Security space.

- Extensive knowledge of full product development life cycle, have experience involving various stages, with demonstrated programming skills in Java, Python, Go or similar.

- Familiar with mainstream development frameworks, common distributed system components, caching, messaging, and other mechanisms.

- Capable of independent system design, with experience in designing, developing, and tuning large-scale distributed, high-concurrency, and high-availability systems.

- Possessing business understanding ability, able to identify problems in business requirements and system architecture design, and provide effective solutions.

- Strong coordination and communication skills, capable of coping with stress, and quickly learning new knowledge.

Nice to Have

- Have experience working in Web3 security companies and developed large-scale API / Monitoring systems.

- Experience with risk control products and relevant experience in developing risk control APIs.

- Basic understanding of common Smart Contract security vulnerabilities, Current on-chain incidents and Wallet Security.

- Basic understanding of blockchain and smart contract principles, experienced with reading Blockchain explorers and creating scripts to track and scan data. Well versed with the different types of hacks on wallets and blockchain, including smart contracts, and its common attack vectors.

 Why Binance 

- Shape the future of finance 

- Collaborate with world-class talent in a user-centric global organization with a flat structure

- Tackle challenging projects in a fast-paced and innovative enviornment with autonomy

Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. HOW YOU'LL MAKE IMPACT

You’ll define the technical direction for Airwallex’s Payments Platform, lead architecture decisions and build highly reliable, high-volume distributed systems that directly affect merchant experience and business outcomes.

You’ll drive complex initiatives across payment gateways, acquiring, issuing, card networks and local payment methods, while partnering with product, business, infrastructure and external engineering teams to turn merchant needs into technical solutions.

jobs.location: New York City, NY | San Francisco, California, United States
jobs.jd:
About Anthropic 

 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the Role 

 Anthropic manages one of the largest and fastest-growing infrastructure fleets in the industry — spanning multiple accelerator families, cpu families and clouds. The Capacity Engineering team is responsible for making sure all our infrastructure resources are accounted for, well-utilized, and efficiently allocated. We own the data, tooling, and operational systems that let Anthropic plan, measure, and maximize utilization across first-party and third-party compute.

 As an engineer on Capacity Engineering, you will build the production systems that power this work: data pipelines that ingest and normalize telemetry from heterogeneous cloud environments, observability tooling that gives the org real-time visibility into fleet health, and performance instrumentation that measures how efficiently every major workload uses the hardware it’s running on. You will be expected to write production-quality code every day, operate alongside Kubernetes-native infrastructure at meaningful scale, and directly influence decisions around one of Anthropic’s largest areas of spend.

 You’ll collaborate closely with research engineering, infrastructure, inference, and finance teams. The work requires someone who can move between data engineering, systems engineering, and observability with comfort — and who thrives in a high-autonomy, high-ambiguity environment.

 This is a pipeline role feeding four areas. Depending on your background and business priority, you’ll focus primarily in one, but the boundaries are fluid and the problems overlap: 

- Data platform Pipelines that ingest occupancy and utilization telemetry from Kubernetes clusters, normalize billing and usage across cloud providers, and serve the BigQuery tables the rest of the org queries against. Correctness, completeness, and latency are the job, not a footnote. Consumers range from research engineers to finance to leadership, so it's product work as much as engineering: defining schema contracts, making data discoverable, and figuring out what people actually need.

- Planning Knowing what the fleet has, where it's going, and what's in the way. Making the state of the fleet legible and actionable in real time: cluster health tooling, capacity planning platforms, alerting on occupancy drops and allocation problems, and systemic fixes to scheduling and fragmentation. Kubernetes operations on one side, cross-team coordination on the other.

- Efficiency Measuring and improving how effectively every major workload uses the hardware it runs on. Instrumenting utilization across training, inference, and eval systems, building benchmarking infrastructure, establishing per-config baselines, and working directly with system-owning teams to close the gaps. The metric has to be good enough that the team on the hook for it agrees with the number.

- Attribution and forecasting Connecting what the fleet costs to what the business is doing with it. Reconciling CSP billing exports against vendor telemetry and internal systems with mismatched schemas, attributing spend to the workloads and teams that generate it, and turning inference demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan. Efficiency metrics have to survive contact with finance: stripped of pure demand and unit-price effects, reproducible month over month, and legible to a CFO.

 Key responsibilities 

- Build the planning and allocation stack — the tools leadership uses to allocate capacity, teams use to plan against their allocations, and the scheduler enforces. Cross-region and cross-provider placement, guardrails, queueing, occupancy KPIs.

- Drive the efficiency programs: stranding and rightsizing, unused capacity recovery, and job-level utilization across training, inference, and eval. Establish per-config baselines and work with system-owning teams to close the gaps. Utilization improvements are worth enormous sums at our scale.

- Own attribution and forecasting — reconcile billing across ten-plus providers against telemetry and internal systems, attribute spend to the workloads that generate it, and turn demand signals and research roadmaps into a defensible compute plan and supply pipeline.

- Build the data platform underneath all of it: pipelines ingesting occupancy, utilization, and cost from a rapidly diversifying fleet into BigQuery, with real ownership of completeness, latency SLOs, and gap detection. Every new provider is a net-new integration.

- Operate Kubernetes-native systems at scale — collection agents, workload labeling, and the taint/reservation/scheduling behavior that determines what capacity is actually usable.

- Treat the output as a product, not a pipeline. Gather your own requirements, define schema contracts, and design for consumers ranging from research engineers to a CFO — including on-call and SLOs, because these surfaces are load-bearing for the company.

 What you bring 

- A strong track record building and operating production systems. This is a hands-on engineering role with a devops flavor.

- Python and SQL at production quality. Most pipeline code is Python; the presentation layer is BigQuery SQL, including table-valued functions and views. Both need to be idiomatic, well-tested, and maintainable.

- Deep experience with at least one major cloud provider (Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Azure) and its operations

- Experience with observability tooling stack, including Prometheus, PromQL, and Grafana, including writing recording rules and building monitoring that engineering teams rely on.

- Ability to gather your own requirements and work across organizational b

 Okta Integration Network (OIN)

In practice that spans connector metadata and provisioning primitives, partner-facing tooling, and the infrastructure work that keeps a very large, long-lived system fast, secure, and easy to extend as the network grows.

 We're actively expanding OIN's scope beyond its original SSO-and-provisioning core — including new integration patterns as AI agents and machine-to-machine access become part of the identity landscape, and a lower-friction path for partners to bring new integrations into the network. You'd be joining at a point where the platform's scope is visibly widening, working closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it.

 Staff Software Engineer, Integration Network (OIN) 

 As a Staff Software Engineer on the OIN team, you'll be a technical leader for a platform a very large share of Okta's customers depend on every day. You'll independently own complex, ambiguous problems end-to-end — from technical scoping through design, delivery, and production operation — partnering closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it. - Drive technical decisions across ambiguous, multi-team dependencies, aligning stakeholders across engineering, product, and other parts of the business when the "right answer" isn't obvious yet.

- Modernize and evolve a large, long-lived production system incrementally without disrupting the customers and integrations that depend on it every day.

- Maintain a high bar for security, testing, and code quality, including vulnerability remediation and threat-aware design, while keeping a real sense of urgency on customer-impacting work.

- Own the production health of the systems you build by writing root-cause analyses when things break, driving follow-through on the fixes, and building the observability that prevents repeat incidents.

- Champion AI-native engineering practices by using AI coding assistants and AI-augmented workflows as a core part of how you design, build, review, and ship software, and helping the team adopt them well.

- Mentor and raise the technical bar for the engineers around you, and represent the team's technical point of view in cross-functional forums.

 What you’ll bring to the role

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Agent Eval Platform
jobs.jd:
The Role 
 Moveworks' AI agents don't just generate text — they act. They plan, call tools, and change real state in enterprise systems on behalf of 5.5 million employees. That makes the central problem of our team an unusually hard measurement problem: how do you score what an agent did — across a multi-step trajectory through a world it changed — precisely enough that the score can teach it to do better? 
 That signal is what this role owns. You'll build the judgement layer of our agent evaluation platform: the rubrics, the judges, the calibration against human labels, the methodology that makes a score mean something. And the payoff is larger than a report card — a judge good enough to grade a trajectory is a judge good enough to train against . The same calibrated signal that explains why an agent failed becomes the reward signal that stops it failing.
 This isn't a pretraining role, and it isn't a testing role. It's applied ML at a point where the methodology genuinely isn't settled: LLMs judging LLMs is an open research problem, and we're working it against agents that take real, irreversible actions in stateful, multi-tenant enterprise environments.

 What you get to do in this role: 
 We're hiring across three areas. You'll anchor on one and touch the others; which one is a conversation we have with you, not a slot we drop you into.
 Eval orchestration at scale 
 
- The runtime that executes multi-turn agent scenarios end-to-end — stand up the environment and user simulator, drive the user↔agent↔world loop, collect transcripts, traces, and final state, run validators and scoring, tear down

- Scheduling, retries, high-concurrency execution, and run isolation at production dataset sizes

- Versioned specs, datasets, and reports, with run-to-run comparison as a first-class operation

- Consolidating evals that run today as one-off workflows onto a single orchestration service — one source of truth, one place to schedule and retry

- Establishing a reliability floor and an SLO for the harness itself

- Getting to self-serve, so any team runs an eval without bespoke integration
 Agent observability and tracing 
 
- Leading the move to OpenTelemetry-native observability for the agent platform, replacing the parallel per-service logging, correlation, and redaction mechanisms in use today

- The span data model for agent trajectories — prompts, tool calls, plan updates, outcomes — so a trajectory is queryable , not reconstructed by hand from log files

- Trace context propagation across async boundaries and sessions that stay alive for minutes or hours

- Making full prompts and completions survive the pipeline intact, and keeping eval traffic from contaminating its own data

- Fault attribution and cross-run diffing: which component actually broke, and what changed since the last green run

- The debug surface support and harness engineers use, and the tracing contract with the team that builds the agent
 Stateful simulation 
 
- The simulation environment itself: stateful fakes of the enterprise systems agents call — ITSM, HR, knowledge bases, inventory — backed by a real datastore that persists changes during a run, so a created ticket is visible to a later read

- Per-run data injection and programmatic setup/teardown so every run is hermetic and repeatable

- LLM-driven user simulators for open-ended personas, and scripted state-machine simulators for deterministic flows

- Contract-testing mocks against real API schemas in CI, so simulation fidelity can't quietly drift as vendor APIs change

- Ahead of us: isolated sandbox environments reproducing the config, identity, search content, and permissions an agent actually reads — provisioned from an identical baseline and torn down every run
 And across all three: laying the foundation for using eval signal to optimize the agent, not just measure it.

To be successful in this role you have: 
 
 Experience in at least 3 of these: 
 
- Distributed systems: idempotency, delivery guarantees, isolation, and — unusually central here — determinism and reproducibility

- Orchestration and workflow runtimes: DAG execution, scheduling, retries, backfills, high-concurrency job systems (Temporal, Airflow, Argo, or something you built yourself)

- Observability internals as a builder , not just a user: OpenTelemetry SDKs and collectors, semantic conventions, span context propagation, high-cardinality trace data

- Concurrent and async programming: Python asyncio, Go concurrency, structured cancellation

- Data-intensive pipelines: high-volume ingest, schema evolution, sampling and retention trade-offs

- gRPC/protobuf service and interface design
 Required: 
 
- 0-2 years building production backend or infrastructure systems

- Strong in Python or Go (ideally both)

- Experience designing and operating systems that handle real traffic at scale

- Comfort making a non-deterministic system measurable. You don't need an ML background — but you should find it interesting to turn fuzzy agent behavior into a signal engineers are willing to gate releases on

- Comfort with ambiguity; these are novel problems without textbook solutions

Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs.

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. You will work across product and data systems to make authorized retrieval and case handling accurate, efficient, and auditable. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys translating ambiguous operational requirements into durable systems, cares deeply about sensitive-data handling, and wants to improve both technical reliability and the day-to-day experience of the people operating these workflows.

 - Design, build, and operate backend systems and workflow tooling for the full lifecycle of lawful data access requests, from intake and scoping through authorized retrieval, review, preparation, and audit.

 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 

 Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.

 Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.

 Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue.

What you’ll do

 As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.

 You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve.

 Responsibilities 

- Build and operate reliable, low-latency services that detect and prevent fraud and abuse at scale

- Design APIs and dashboard experiences that help businesses investigate threats, configure defenses, and understand how Radar protects them

- Develop the shared platform and infrastructure that enable teams to build and launch new Radar capabilities

- Work directly with users to understand emerging threats and turn those insights into broadly useful products

- Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to bring new signals, models, and AI capabilities into production

- Uphold a high bar for engineering quality, reliability, and product craft while moving quickly as threats evolve

 Minimum requirements

- An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems

 Preferred qualifications 

- Experience building distributed systems or real-time services with demanding reliability and latency requirements

- Experience building APIs, developer platforms, or intuitive user interfaces for complex workflows

- Experience bringing ML or AI capabilities into production software

- Experience working on fraud prevention, abuse prevention, risk, or security

- Experience taking a product from an early idea to launch and iterating directly with customers
